notes: SHIP v1.14.399 - M1-c: EVERY WRITE PATH IS GUARDED, AND PDF IMPORT WORKS OFFLINE. Fourth data-safety ship. .397 and .398 made sure a backup CONTAINS the work; this one makes sure the work gets WRITTEN in the first place, and that the last online-only vendor path stops being online-only. ST1 - THE HIGHEST DATA-LOSS EXPOSURE IN THE APP. A private store wrapper backed phantom_node_status_v1, which holds per-node racked/pending state - real work a technician did in the aisle - plus the two Forge loadout keys. Its set() was try { localStorage.setItem(...) } catch (e) {} - a NAKED catch. On a quota-full device the write failed, NOTHING WAS SAID, and the tech kept marking nodes racked against a store that had quietly stopped recording. Both halves now route through the hardened layer: get through safeParse, set through safeStore, which classifies the quota signature and raises the throttled Storage full toast. setStatus checks the result and logs the specific node whose status did not persist, so a later I-marked-that-racked dispute has evidence instead of a shrug. ST2 - THE TWO UNGUARDED WRITES. bom_classify_saveOverride and bom_classify_clearOverride were the only two localStorage.setItem calls in the file with no guard at all, so on a quota-full or storage-disabled device the exception propagated straight out of the function. Both now go through safeStore and return false instead of throwing. These are hand-entered classifier corrections for field-discovered typo classes - not re-derivable, which is why they matter. ST3 - A READ-SIDE WHITELIST. ge_load carried the comment graceful merge if new fields are added later and did the exact opposite: it rebuilt a literal with three named fields and dropped everything else. Paired with ge_save, which writes back whatever ge_load returned, the ROUND-TRIP ERASED any field the function did not name. Same defect class as the documented MASTER_STORE.save whitelist, but on the READ side, where nobody is looking for it. Now Object.assign preserves the stored object first, then normalises the three fields it knows. ST5 - OFFLINE PDF IMPORT. vendor/pdf.min.js and vendor/pdf.worker.min.js were loaded at runtime via loadScript() and were absent from the service worker precache list, so an offline import failed with Check connection and retry - honest, and wrong for an offline-first field app. Both are precached now. COST STATED PLAINLY: +1.5 MB on install, of which pdf.worker is 1.1 MB, taking the total precache from roughly 7.3 MB to 8.81 MB. That is paid once on a good connection so a tech in a cold aisle with no signal can still import a document. VERIFIED BEFORE SHIP: all 56 precache entries exist on disk, no duplicates, both pdf files present. Note that the first run of that check reported a phantom missing entry - the regex was pulling a quoted string out of a COMMENT rather than the array, and was corrected before it could be believed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean x3, sw.js compiles, CSS braces 4557/4557, line endings preserved, three-stamp lockstep. REMAINING IN M1: safeGet and safeRemove (neither exists, so 121 getItem and 31 removeItem calls are still raw by construction) and the corrupt-data quarantine path, which pair together as the read-side ship. The six dead else localStorage.setItem arms (ST6) are catalogued and deliberately deferred - they are unreachable, since safeStore is declared above all of them. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) mark a node racked in the aisle view, reload, confirm it persisted. (2) With DevTools storage throttled or a nearly-full device, mark a node and confirm a Storage full toast appears rather than silence. (3) Go fully offline and import a PDF - it should work with no connection prompt.
